html:
The Okwanuchu were a small Native American people of northern California, living on the upper Sacramento and McCloud rivers south of Mount Shasta. They spoke a Shastan language and were close relatives of the larger Shasta people to the north.

Very little is known of them. They lived by fishing for salmon, hunting and gathering acorns. Settlers and miners arrived in the 1850s, after the Gold Rush, and the Okwanuchu soon vanished as a separate group; survivors probably joined neighbouring peoples such as the Achumawi and the Wintu.
